cases_doc: D.3 calibration slate — mafft msa_alignment. NARROWEST claim: descriptive, never 'correct' (C1-hole M4). Scoped carefully so no IN case smuggles a correctness claim.
label_provenance: pre-registered by the build chat 2026-07-19 from the ruled card (M1-M4); in->trust, out->defer.
substrate_text: MAFFT MULTIPLE SEQUENCE ALIGNMENT: it arranges >=2 same-alphabet sequences into columns of putative homology. This carries the NARROWEST trust claim of the wave. Returns alignment_identity (the average pairwise percent identity over the computed alignment), DESCRIPTIVE only. Input that is not alignable (fewer than 2 sequences, mixed alphabets, invalid residues) is refused before running. THE KNOWN GAP (M4, the whole scientific question): a computed alignment is a HEURISTIC homology hypothesis, guide-tree-dependent — a different tool or setting gives a different alignment. The trust claim is 'an alignment MAFFT COMPUTED, well-formed, used DESCRIPTIVELY', NEVER 'the CORRECT or biologically-true alignment'.
envelope_text: IN-REGIME: >=2 genuinely alignable same-alphabet sequences; the alignment and its identity statistic used PURELY DESCRIPTIVELY (what MAFFT computed). OUT-OF-REGIME: any claim that the alignment is the CORRECT / biologically-true / evolutionarily-accurate one; a claim of structural or functional correctness of the aligned columns; treating the heuristic alignment as ground-truth homology.

gate_cases.experiment: Align three closely-related protein sequences with MAFFT and report the resulting average pairwise percent identity as a DESCRIPTIVE statistic of the alignment MAFFT computed.
gate_cases.note: Dead-centre and DESCRIPTIVE: alignable sequences, the statistic framed as 'what MAFFT computed' — never as correctness.
gate_cases.right_instrument: the alignment MAFFT computed, described by its pairwise identity.

gate_cases.experiment: Align a set of four homologous protein sequences and report the computed multiple alignment together with its average pairwise identity, as MAFFT's computed output.
gate_cases.note: In-regime, descriptive: the computed alignment reported as the tool's output, no correctness claim.

gate_cases.experiment: Align two protein sequences with MAFFT and report the percent identity over the aligned non-gap columns as a descriptive similarity summary of the computed alignment.
gate_cases.note: In-regime, descriptive: a 2-sequence alignment summarized by its computed identity.
gate_cases.right_instrument: the computed pairwise alignment, summarized descriptively.

gate_cases.experiment: Align several nucleotide sequences of the same gene and report the computed alignment's average pairwise identity as a descriptive measure of how similar the sequences are as aligned.
gate_cases.note: In-regime, descriptive: same-alphabet nucleotides, the identity used descriptively.
gate_cases.right_instrument: the computed nucleotide alignment, described by its identity.

gate_cases.experiment: Report that MAFFT produced a well-formed alignment of five same-alphabet sequences with a given average pairwise identity, as the computed result to be used descriptively downstream.
gate_cases.note: In-regime, descriptive: explicitly 'the computed result, used descriptively' — the exact narrow trust framing.
gate_cases.right_instrument: the well-formed alignment MAFFT computed, for descriptive use.

gate_cases.experiment: Report the MAFFT alignment as the CORRECT, biologically-true alignment of the sequences (the definitive column-by-column homology).
gate_cases.note: C1-hole M4, direct: a correctness claim. The alignment is a heuristic hypothesis, never 'the correct' one.
gate_cases.right_instrument: a structural/curated benchmark alignment — not a heuristic MAFFT alignment.

gate_cases.experiment: Use the MAFFT alignment's aligned columns as ground-truth evidence that two specific residues are evolutionarily HOMOLOGOUS positions.
gate_cases.note: C1-hole M4: treating heuristic aligned columns as established positional homology is a correctness claim.
gate_cases.right_instrument: a structure/phylogeny-validated homology assignment — not a heuristic alignment.

gate_cases.experiment: Conclude from the MAFFT alignment that the aligned regions are STRUCTURALLY equivalent in the folded proteins.
gate_cases.note: C1-hole M4: a structural-correctness claim; sequence alignment does not establish structural equivalence.
gate_cases.right_instrument: a structural alignment (superposition) — not a sequence alignment.

gate_cases.experiment: Report the MAFFT alignment as the definitive input for phylogenetic tree inference, treating its columns as the TRUE evolutionary history.
gate_cases.note: C1-hole M4: treating the heuristic, guide-tree-dependent alignment as true evolutionary history is a correctness claim.
gate_cases.right_instrument: a correctness-validated / multiple-method alignment — not a single heuristic run.

gate_cases.experiment: State that because MAFFT produced a high-identity alignment, the alignment is therefore the RIGHT alignment (identity proves correctness).
gate_cases.note: C1-hole M4: high identity is descriptive; it does not prove the alignment is correct. This conflates well-formed with correct.
gate_cases.right_instrument: a benchmarked correctness assessment — identity does not prove correctness.

wrapper_cases.note: Single sequence refused pre-run (not an alignment).
